# `mise generate install-script`

- **Usage:** `mise generate install-script [FLAGS]`
- **Effect:** modifies state
- **Source code:** [`src/cli/generate/install_script.rs`](https://github.com/jdx/mise/blob/main/src/cli/generate/install_script.rs)

Generate a script that downloads and runs a pinned mise

Commit the script, for example as bin/mise, so contributors and CI can run
`./bin/mise install` without installing mise first. On first run it downloads
the pinned mise version into the mise data directory, or into the project with
--localize, then runs it with the arguments it was given.

`mise generate bootstrap` is a deprecated alias for this command and will be
removed in mise 2027.9.0.

## Flags
- **`-l --localize`** — Keep mise data and cache in a project-local directory (`.mise` by default)

  Use `--localized-dir` to choose its location. This isolates mise state;
  it is not an OS sandbox for commands the generated script runs.
- **`-V --version <VERSION>`** — mise version to pin; defaults to the release `mise self-update` would install
- **`-w --write [PATH]`** — Write the script to PATH (./bin/mise when no path is given) and make it executable, instead of printing it
- **`--localized-dir <DIR>`** — Directory for mise data when using --localize, relative to the project

  **Default:** `.mise`
- **`--windows`** — Also write a Windows launcher, `<PATH>.cmd`

  Windows cannot run the bash script. Generate the launcher on any OS and commit
  it for contributors on Windows. Requires --write.
- **`-h --help`** — Print help

## Examples

Write ./bin/mise; on first run it downloads the pinned mise, then runs it

```
mise generate install-script --write ./bin/mise
```

Keep mise and its tools in .mise inside the project

```
mise generate install-script --localize --write ./bin/mise
```

Also write bin/mise.cmd for contributors on Windows

```
mise generate install-script --write ./bin/mise --windows
```
